newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich ethics woes stemmed from college course.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich ethics woes stemmed from college course.

text.p: The charges that brought a reprimand and $300,000 penalty for House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich stemmed from a college course he taught called "Renewing American Civilisation."
The House ethics committee found that the course, devised in the early 1990s, was aimed at winning Republican control of the House.

When his former political action committee, known as GOPAC, no longer had enough money to disseminate the course, Gingrich arranged for funding by three tax-exempt foundations which under the law are barred from partisan political activity, the committee said.
Under an agreement last December with an ethics subcommittee investigating the case, Gingrich acknowledged only that he did not seek legal advice to ensure compliance with the tax laws.
The subcommitee said its expert and Gingrich's tax counsel agreed that if they had been consulted they would have advised against using a tax-exempt organisation.

the subcommittee's report issued last week said that either Gingrich did not seek legal advice because he knew he would be barred from use of a tax-exempt organisation or he was "reckless" in not taking care to comply with the law.
The subcommittee also found that Gingrich had provided investigators with information in two letters regarding the courses that he "should have known was inaccurate, incomplete and unreliable."
"Both letters were efforts by Mr Gingrich to have the committee dismiss the complaints without further inquiry," the report said.
Gingrich said that he did not intentionally provide false information and the subcommittee said the record was not conclusive on this point.

"Either Mr Gingrich's conduct in regard to the (tax-exempt) organisations and the letters he submitted to the committee was intentional or it was reckless," the report said. "Neither choice reflects creditably on the House."
The report also said that there had been an apparent violation of an agreement by Gingrich in December not to make public comment about the ethics matter while it was pending.
